- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in short-term (1–7 days) — adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8), model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.  
- When sentiment is uniformly high and price is flat or slightly rising, model often overreacts — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven inflation.”
